chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about the purchase of unthreshed grain (al-qasil). A man buys it but does not thresh it, and it seems good to him to leave it until its ear emerges as barley or wheat. He had bought it from its owner while the land tax (kharaj) was upon its owners, or it was upon the 'Ajl (non-Muslims). He said: 'If he stipulated at the time of purchase that he may cut it if he wishes, or leave it as it is until it becomes an ear, then that is permissible; otherwise, it is not fitting for him to leave it until it becomes an ear.'

key_terms.الْعِلْجِ: Non-Muslims (specifically in the context of land tax in early Islamic Iraq)
key_terms.الْقَصِيلِ: Unthreshed grain still in the stalk
key_terms.يَقْصِلُهُ: To thresh or process the unthreshed grain

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for leaving unthreshed grain in the field after purchase according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the contractual freedom in selling unthreshed grain (*qasil*), establishing that the buyer's right to delay threshing until the grain becomes a full ear (*sunbul*) depends on explicit stipulation at the time of purchase. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that ambiguity in the condition of delivery or processing must be resolved by the explicit agreement of the parties, preventing arbitrary retention of goods. This ruling ensures fairness in agricultural trade by distinguishing between a sale where early harvest is optional versus one where waiting for maturity is the default obligation.
